_doc: Prompts for tools/music/eleven.py. kind: sfx (one-shot), amb (looping ambience), music. See docs/AUDIO_PLAN.md.
music_style: Instrumental, period-authentic 18th century colonial America, acoustic instruments only, recorded in a warm wooden room, no synths, no modern drums, no vocals, gentle dynamics, suitable as background music for a relaxing strategy game.

items.prompt: A single strike of a huge old bronze church bell, deep fundamental with a slightly cracked, buzzing overtone, long natural decay in open air, 18th century town square. No music.
A wooden gavel struck twice on a desk in a large wooden assembly hall, then a small brass handbell rung once, warm room reverb.
A ship's brass bell struck twice quickly, ding-ding, on a wooden sailing ship at harbour, light wind.
Melted sealing wax pressed with a brass seal stamp onto thick parchment, soft squish and firm thud, close-up foley.
A few gold coins dropped onto a wooden counter, bright clinks, close and dry.
A small handful of coins poured into a leather purse, quick and soft.
A heavy locked wooden chest lid rattled once against its iron latch, short dull thunk.
A single light tap of a wooden quill holder on a writing desk, very short, dry, close.
A single page of thick old parchment turned quickly, crisp, close.
A heavy leather-bound book closed firmly, then a harpsichord plays a short bright rising three-note figure.
An old almanac opened and a page turned, followed by a soft two-note glockenspiel chime.
A wooden stake hammered into earth three times with a mallet, then a short bright fife flourish.
A wooden crate lid pried open with a creak, then a short bright pizzicato string flourish.
A short ascending glockenspiel chime over a soft harp chord, baroque, bright and celebratory.
A dusty wooden chest creaks open, then a shimmering harp arpeggio blooms into a warm chord.
A quick ascending wooden flute run over pizzicato strings, 18th century chamber style, cheerful.
A short royal fanfare on natural baroque trumpets and horns with timpani rolls, 18th century court, triumphant ending chord.
A joyful peal of church bells over warm strings and a harpsichord, celebratory, ending on a held chord.
A goose-feather quill scratching quickly across rough parchment, one short stroke, close-up.
A waterlogged wooden chest dragged onto a deck and forced open, coins spilling out.
A loose sheet of old paper caught by the wind and snatched from the air, soft rustle, a small bright chime.
A carpenter's saw stroke and two hammer blows on timber in a busy workshop, then silence.
A large sheet of heavy parchment slid quickly across a wooden table, soft swish.
A large sheet of heavy parchment slid slowly across a wooden table, soft low swish.
A ceremonial sword tapped twice on a wooden table, then a short murmur of approval from a few people.
Distant 18th century cannon salute, three booms rolling across a harbour, with cheering crowd far away.
A heavy door opening onto a busy colonial street, a rooster crows in the distance, coins jingle in a pocket.
Gentle coastal wilderness: soft waves on a sandy shore, distant gulls, songbirds in a forest, a far-off axe chopping wood now and then. Calm, no music.
18th century harbour: water lapping against wooden hulls, creaking ropes and rigging, gulls, distant dockside chatter, a far bell. No music.
Quiet wooden assembly hall: soft room tone, an old clock ticking slowly, an occasional quill scratch and paper rustle, faint muffled voices. No music.
Fife and snare drum march, unhurried, then joined by a fiddle; optimistic morning in a new settlement. Ends with a clear final cadence.
Solo fiddle air, slow and tender, with a cello drone; dusk over a river valley. Ends with a clear final cadence.
Lively jig on fiddle, wooden flute and hand drum; a harvest day. Ends with a clear final cadence.
Harpsichord and recorder duet, light and stately; a colonial governor's garden. Ends with a clear final cadence.
Hammered dulcimer and fiddle, mid-tempo, warm and pastoral; a frontier homestead. Ends with a clear final cadence.
Bustling 18th century London harbour tune: sea-shanty-flavoured fiddle, wooden flute and hand drum. Ends with a clear final cadence.
A stately baroque string quartet for a merchant's counting house in 18th century London. Ends with a clear final cadence.
A lilting sailor's hornpipe on fiddle and wooden flute, cheerful, dockside. Ends with a clear final cadence.
A harpsichord-and-strings minuet for a solemn 18th century assembly hall, dignified. Ends with a clear final cadence.
A slow processional for chamber organ and strings, solemn and hopeful. Ends with a clear final cadence.
A thoughtful baroque string trio, measured and reflective, statesmen deliberating. Ends with a clear final cadence.
Triumphant fife-and-drum march building into full natural brass, timpani and pealing church bells, ending on a big held chord. Celebratory, not gentle.
